candidates.label: Tekanan kondisi jalan: persentase panjang jalan tidak mantap/rusak
candidates.institution: Dinas Bina Marga dan Penataan Ruang Provinsi Jawa Barat; Badan Pusat Statistik Provinsi Jawa Barat
candidates.coverage: Galura response contained 864 records across 2018–2025. Actual 2023 inspection covered all 27 Jawa Barat kabupaten/kota: 18 kabupaten (3201–3218) and nine kota (3271–3279), with 108 records, exactly four conditions per region. Geographic presence is complete, but this UPTD-managed network is not a comparable measure of all district/city roads. BPS 2024 yearbook tables 9.1.1 and 9.1.4 also display all 27 regions; their authority and condition lengths do not reconcile consistently. Coverage of every other year was not independently audited region by region.
candidates.unit: Source: KILOMETER; proposed percentage not calculated
candidates.definition: Proposed pressure is non-mantap/damaged road length divided by total road length within the same year, geography, and road-authority network. Galura defines MANTAP as BAIK plus SEDANG and TIDAK MANTAP as RUSAK RINGAN plus RUSAK BERAT. Its records describe road length by kabupaten/kota and six UPTD road-and-bridge service areas. A region location is not the same as district/city road ownership; the condition table has no kewenangan_pemerintah field.
candidates.reason: Actual records exist for all 27 regions, but eligibility fails on road-network scope and denominator comparability, not data absence. UPTD condition lengths track the provincial managed network rather than the district/city network. A checked Subang discrepancy and inconsistent BPS authority-versus-condition totals prevent a defensible common denominator. Retain source metadata and quality findings only; do not score, merge national/provincial/district roads, or publish a fabricated damaged-road percentage.
limitations: Road responsibility differs among national, provincial, and kabupaten/kota networks. Province-managed road conditions located within a district do not measure the condition of roads administered by that district.

Galura describes UPTD service areas and condition categories, but its condition records lack an explicit authority variable. The related authority dataset was located and its metadata inspected; a full authority-response reconciliation was not completed.

The derived 2023 Subang sum of Galura's four condition lengths is 45.68 km; BPS table 9.1.1 reports 167.86 km of provincial roads there. The difference is unresolved and must not be hidden by substituting another authority's total.

For Subang, BPS table 9.1.4's four 2023 condition lengths sum to 1,319.864 km, while table 9.1.1 reports 1,365.72 km in its all-authority total and 1,152.00 km in its kabupaten/kota column. The condition table does not explicitly resolve this scope difference.

BPS 2023 road tables mark values as preliminary. Table 9.1.1 excludes toll roads and supplies separate national, provincial, and kabupaten/kota columns. The condition table cannot be treated as an interchangeable denominator without reconciliation.
Complete region codes and nonnegative numeric cells do not establish comparable road-network coverage, stable measurement rules, or suitability as a public-service pressure score.

Galura's usage terms, updated 2026-05-04, grant limited personal non-commercial use without sublicensing and restrict third-party/commercial use absent Diskominfo permission. No permission was obtained. No original response, numeric observation rows, reconstructed regional series, or derived road percentages are redistributed here. Diagnostic summaries and response fingerprints are retained only for the source-quality audit.

candidates.institution: Badan Penanggulangan Bencana Daerah Provinsi Jawa Barat; Badan Nasional Penanggulangan Bencana; Badan Pusat Statistik Provinsi Jawa Barat
candidates.coverage: Galura response contained 1890 records across 2012–2025. Actual 2023 inspection covered all 27 Jawa Barat kabupaten/kota: 18 kabupaten (3201–3218) and nine kota (3271–3279), with 135 records, five outcome categories per region. BPS table 4.5.7 displays all 27 regions by disaster type for 2023. The BNPB book's inspected appendix supplies provincial comparisons; a separate all-27 BNPB machine-readable series was not acquired. Coverage of every other Galura year was not independently audited region by region.
candidates.unit: Source: JIWA, separate outcome counts; proposed rate per 100000 residents not calculated
candidates.definition: Proposed disaster pressure requires a clearly defined person outcome and a matching population denominator. BPBD/Galura distinguishes MENINGGAL DUNIA, HILANG, LUKA-LUKA, MENDERITA, and MENGUNGSI. Its description defines affected/suffering, missing, dead, injured, and evacuated conditions separately. BPS/BNPB instead publishes combined meninggal dan hilang and terdampak/mengungsi categories alongside injured counts, by disaster type. These counts are not an established count of unique residents affected during the year.
candidates.reason: Actual all-27 BPBD data are available, but cross-source outcome totals differ materially and metadata does not resolve repeated persons, overlap among outcomes, event inclusion, reporting completeness, or revision cutoffs. Dividing by population would not repair those problems. Retain contextual metadata and the source-quality audit; do not sum incompatible outcomes or publish a synthetic per-100000 pressure score.
limitations: Source definitions do not establish whether a person affected by several events is counted once or repeatedly, or whether injured, evacuated, affected, missing, and deceased groups overlap. Do not add the five outcome categories into a victim total.

BPBD/Galura and BNPB/BPS are different reporting series, not interchangeable measurements. Their 2023 province-level diagnostic totals do not reconcile; no authoritative reconciliation or common reporting cutoff was found in the inspected metadata.

Galura calls tahun the production year. The inspected description does not establish a common event-reference window, occurrence-versus-report date rule, inclusion/exclusion rules, or the completeness of reporting for each region.

The 27-region presence check is geographic coverage, not evidence that every event or affected person was reported. Numeric zeros cannot be converted into proof of no disaster impact or complete surveillance.

BPS table 4.5.7 presents separate disaster types and combined outcome labels. Its dash, zero and unavailable symbols require separate interpretation; no missing observation was silently imputed as zero.

BNPB's inspected book points to a QR-linked district/city companion, but that statement alone does not prove retrieval of a reconciled all-27 2023 series. The inspected national appendix contains province rows, not the required district/city observation artifact.

No population join or per-100000 rate was created. Resident-population rates would remain event-affected-person rates unless deduplication and outcome scope were established; they must not be labelled the percentage of unique residents harmed.

Galura's usage terms permit limited personal non-commercial use without sublicensing, absent additional permission. BNPB's book also states reproduction/quotation requires written permission. No original responses, numeric regional rows, book excerpts, or derived regional rates are redistributed. Only source metadata, response fingerprints, and diagnostic audit summaries are retained.
